title: Predictive-reserve autoscale + controlled soft-shrink for multi-zone dedicated pools under residency constraints
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers running multi-zone dedicated fleets need predictable throughput and non-disruptive capacity changes while also satisfying strict regional/data-residency constraints. Current autoscaler can add capacity reactively but: (a) often overshoots under bursty workloads causing cost spikes, and (b) tears down capacity immediately on scale-in which can violate soft-SLOs for request latency. We also lack a clear mechanism to ensure residency locks during aggressive autoscale operations across zones.

Proposal: Implement a predictive-reserve autoscaling mode that allocates a small, time-windowed reserve based on short-term forecasts and recent tail-latency signals, paired with a configurable "soft-shrink" workflow for scale-in that drains capacity gradually (evicting new allocations first, migrating existing KV cache prefixes off the node, and reducing offered slots in steps). Enforce residency constraints by introducing per-pool residency-locks that prevent scale-in from crossing the pool's allowed-region affinity unless migration policies are explicitly invoked. Expose new Dedicated configuration fields (reserve_mode, reserve_window_sec, soft_shrink_steps, residency_lock) in the Dedicated API and console.
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated API accepts new config fields: reserve_mode=(predictive|none), reserve_window_sec=integer, soft_shrink_steps=integer, residency_lock=(regional|none).

Under synthetic burst tests (replica of customer workload), the predictive-reserve path keeps 95th latency <= baseline+15% during burst from 100rps->2000rps without >20% overshoot in active provisioned GPUs compared to reactive mode.
Soft-shrink drains nodes in configurable steps with no 5xx error increase attributable to eviction; automated integration test verifies request success rate stays >=99.5% during scale-in scenarios.
Residency-lock prevents allocation of scaled-down capacity from moving workloads out of the configured region; audit logs record any manual override operations.
Console shows new dashboard panels: reserve utilization, shrink-step progress, residency-lock violations, and cost delta estimates for predictive reserves.
End-to-end canary rollout plan executed with one customer-account group (canary) and no regression incidents for 48 hours before broader rollout.

decision_log: 2025-02-14: Chose predictive-reserve approach instead of static overprovision because forecasting + small reserve reduces median cost while protecting tail latency. (Decision owners: Diego, Priya)

2025-02-18: For forecasting algorithm we will ship with EWMA + burst-detect heuristic for v1 due to predictability and low compute; leave room to replace with TS model if telemetry shows >10% miss rate. (Decision owners: Priya, SRE)

2025-02-20: Soft-shrink will be default for scale-in when residency_lock is set to regional; immediate-evict remains an opt-in flag for emergency drain. This prevents accidental cross-region eviction. (Decision owners: Diego, Malik)

2025-02-24: Residency-lock enforcement will be in the orchestrator with both hard checks and soft audit logs for operator overrides; overrides require an approval tagging flow from Console. (Decision owners: Security, Ops)

2025-02-27: Telemetry granularity settled at 5s ingestion for key throughput/latency signals to feed the predictive model; trade-off accepted for slightly higher ingestion cost. (Decision owners: Observability)

risks: Forecast miss risk: if burst patterns are non-stationary, predictive reserve may underprovision and increase latency. Mitigation: emergency immediate-scale path + conservative default reserve_window_sec.

Residency complexity: gradual shrink could require cross-zone cache migration which may temporarily increase network egress and prolong shrink windows. Mitigation: rate-limited migration and cost estimate in console.
Operational complexity: new knobs increase blast radius for operators; mitigation: guarded Console controls, default safe values, and approval-gated overrides.
Telemetry cost: increased ingestion granularity increases observability costs; mitigation: sample on non-canary fleets and roll to all only after telemetry budget approval.
test_plan: Unit tests for new API schema validation and parameter edge-cases.
Integration: synthetic storm from 50rps->3k rps with and without predictive reserves; compare provisioned GPUs and latency percentiles.
Canary: enable reserve_mode=predictive + soft_shrink_steps=5 for 3 customer accounts for 48 hours, monitor SLOs and cost delta.
Chaos: simulate zone failure during soft-shrink to validate that residency-lock prevents cross-region migration and triggers fallback lanes.
Performance: ensure autoscaler decision loop adds <200ms overhead at 5s telemetry cadence.
Audit: verify audit log entries for any manual override of residency_lock and that approvals show up in Console.
notes: We must coordinate with legal for any customer whose residency contracts disallow even temporary cross-region cache migration — those fleets will default to strict residency_lock=regional and immediate-evict disabled. Customer-facing naming for the feature should avoid the term 'autoscale gamble' and instead use 'predictive reserve' in documentation.
observability_requirements: New metrics: reserve_allocated_gpus, reserve_utilization_ratio, shrink_step_progress (per-node), residency_lock_override_count. Alerts: reserve_utilization > 0.8 for >2min (warning), unexpected residency_lock_override (pager).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary on staging clusters. Phase 2: opt-in customer canary (3 customers) for 48h with SRE oversight. Phase 3: gradual rollout to 25% of fleets; monitor cost and latency deltas for 7 days. Phase 4: full rollout behind feature flag and update templates.
customer_communication: Drafted release notes and best-practice guide for configuring reserve_window_sec and soft_shrink_steps. Templates for recommended values by workload class (latency-sensitive, throughput-batched, embedding-only) included in Docs link.
